-- DIMENSION: one row per calendar day. It needs no input table: dbt builds the days itself.
-- The first and last day come from dbt_project.yml (date_start, date_end).

with days as (
    select explode(sequence(to_date('2024-01-01'), to_date('2028-12-31'), interval 1 day)) as full_date
)

select
    cast(date_format(full_date, 'yyyyMMdd') as int) as date_key,     -- 20261007 for 7 October 2026
    full_date,
    year(full_date) as year,
    quarter(full_date) as quarter,
    month(full_date) as month,
    date_format(full_date, 'MMMM') as month_name,
    date_format(full_date, 'yyyy-MM') as year_month,
    day(full_date) as day,
    dayofweek(full_date) as day_of_week,
    date_format(full_date, 'EEEE') as day_name,
    dayofweek(full_date) in (1, 7) as is_weekend
from days

-- DIMENSION: one row per plan VERSION (a plan keeps one row each time its price or limits change).
-- Input: silver.plan_history

-- Part 1: all real plan versions
select

    plan_id,

from `data_sentinel`.`silver`.`plan_history`

-- Part 2: one special row, key -1, for "plan unknown".

    timestamp'1970-01-01 00:00:00',
    timestamp'9999-12-31 00:00:00',

-- Dashboard 1: pass rate per day, dataset and quality dimension (gate rules only).
select
    to_date(run_ts) as run_date,
    dataset,
    dimension,
    sum(rows_checked) as rows_checked,
    sum(rows_failed) as rows_failed,
    1 - sum(rows_failed) / nullif(sum(rows_checked), 0) as pass_rate
from `data_sentinel`.`monitoring`.`dq_results`
where check_name = 'gate_rule'
group by to_date(run_ts), dataset, dimension

-- Dashboard 1: the latest result of every gate rule and monitor (one row per dataset / check / rule / scope).
with ranked as (
    select
        *, row_number() over (partition by dataset, check_name, rule_id, scope order by run_ts desc) as _rn
    from `data_sentinel`.`monitoring`.`dq_results`
)
select
    dataset, check_name, rule_id, dimension, scope, rows_checked, rows_failed, pass_rate, status, severity, detail,
    contract_version, run_id, run_ts
from ranked
where _rn = 1

-- Dashboard 1: incidents with owner, priority, deadline, acknowledgement and SLA status.
-- Needs the incident phase (notebooks 70 and 71) to have run once, so monitoring.incident_ops exists.
select
    i.incident_id, i.dataset, i.check_name, i.pillar, i.severity, i.scope, i.description, i.impacted, i.status,
    i.opened_at, i.closed_at,
    o.priority, o.team, o.owner, o.due_at, o.acknowledged_at, o.acknowledged_by,
    coalesce(o.escalation_level, 0) as escalation_level,
    round((unix_timestamp(coalesce(i.closed_at, current_timestamp())) - unix_timestamp(i.opened_at)) / 3600.0, 2) as open_hours,
    round((unix_timestamp(o.acknowledged_at) - unix_timestamp(i.opened_at)) / 60.0, 1) as minutes_to_ack,
    case
        when i.status = 'RESOLVED' and i.closed_at <= o.due_at then 'RESOLVED_IN_SLA'
        when i.status = 'RESOLVED' then 'RESOLVED_LATE'
        when o.due_at is null then 'UNASSIGNED'
        when current_timestamp() > o.due_at then 'BREACHED'
        else 'ON_TRACK'
    end as sla_status
from `data_sentinel`.`monitoring`.`incidents` i
left join `data_sentinel`.`monitoring`.`incident_ops` o on i.incident_id = o.incident_id

-- Dashboard 2: the latest reconciliation run, one row per check, with the EUR at risk.
with last_run as (
    select run_id from `data_sentinel`.`monitoring`.`recon_results` order by run_ts desc limit 1
)
select
    r.check_id, r.check_name, r.source_a, r.source_b, r.rows_checked, r.rows_mismatched, r.amount_at_risk_eur,
    r.status, r.severity, r.detail, r.run_id, r.run_ts,
    case r.check_id
        when 'R1' then 'Unbilled customer'
        when 'R2' then 'Billing without customer'
        when 'R3' then 'Invoice arithmetic'
        when 'R4' then 'Payment mismatch'
        when 'R5' then 'Wrong plan price'
        when 'R6' then 'File vs database'
        when 'R7' then 'Unmatched payment'
        when 'R8' then 'Unregistered network usage'
        when 'R9' then 'Unregistered partner usage'
        when 'R10' then 'Unpaid invoices'
    end as leak_type,
    r.check_id <> 'R10' as is_data_defect
from `data_sentinel`.`monitoring`.`recon_results` r
join last_run l on r.run_id = l.run_id

-- Dashboard 2: the individual mismatches of the latest run (what the billing team investigates).

-- STAGING: payments from the billing database AND from the monthly billing file, in one list.
-- The column "source" says where each row came from.

select
    'billing_db' as source,
    payment_id, invoice_id, amount, method, status, paid_at
from `data_sentinel`.`silver`.`payment`

union all

select
    'billing_file' as source,
    payment_id, invoice_id, amount, method, status, paid_at
from `data_sentinel`.`silver`.`payment_file`

-- STAGING: invoices from the billing database AND from the monthly billing file, in one list.
-- The column "source" says where each row came from. The reconciliation compares the two sources.
-- Inputs: silver.account, silver.invoice_line, silver.invoice, silver.invoice_file

-- Step 1: the accounts (we need the phone number and account id)
with account as (
    select account_id, account_ref, msisdn_hash
    from `data_sentinel`.`silver`.`account`
),

-- Step 2: add up the lines of each invoice
invoice_lines as (
    select
        invoice_id,
        sum(amount) as lines_total,
        count(*) as lines_count
    from `data_sentinel`.`silver`.`invoice_line`
    group by invoice_id
),

-- Step 3: one account_id per account_ref (the billing file only has the reference)
account_by_ref as (
    select account_ref, min(account_id) as account_id
    from account
    group by account_ref
),

-- Step 4: invoices from the billing database
db_invoices as (
    select
        'billing_db' as source,
        i.invoice_id,
        i.account_id,
        a.account_ref,
        a.msisdn_hash,
        i.period_start,
        i.period_end,
        cast(null as decimal(10,2)) as plan_fee,
        cast(null as decimal(10,2)) as overage,
        i.total_amount,
        i.status,
        i.issued_at,
        l.lines_total,
        l.lines_count
    from `data_sentinel`.`silver`.`invoice` i
    left join account a on i.account_id = a.account_id
    left join invoice_lines l on i.invoice_id = l.invoice_id
),

-- Step 5: invoices from the billing file
file_invoices as (
    select
        'billing_file' as source,
        f.invoice_id,
        r.account_id,
        f.account_ref,
        f.msisdn_hash,
        f.period_start,
        f.period_end,
        f.plan_fee,
        f.overage,
        f.total_amount,
        f.status,
        cast(null as timestamp) as issued_at,
        cast(null as decimal(10,2)) as lines_total,
        cast(null as bigint) as lines_count
    from `data_sentinel`.`silver`.`invoice_file` f
    left join account_by_ref r on f.account_ref = r.account_ref
)

-- Step 6: put both lists together
select * from db_invoices
union all
select * from file_invoices

-- Inputs: silver.customer_history (the customers) and dim_plan (the plan prices).
-- Only masked or hashed personal data is here. Raw phone, email and name never reach Gold.

-- Part 1: all real customer versions
select
    xxhash64(c.customer_id, c.valid_from) as customer_key,   -- a unique number made from customer_id + start date
    c.customer_id,
    c.version,
    c.valid_from,
    c.valid_to,
    c.is_current,
    c.name_masked,
    c.email_masked,
    c.email_hash,
    c.msisdn_masked,
    c.msisdn_hash,
    c.city,
    c.country,
    c.status,
    c.plan_id,
    -- plan_key: first choice = the plan version that was valid when this customer version started,
    --           second choice = the current plan, last choice = -1 (unknown)
    coalesce(p.plan_key, cp.plan_key, -1) as plan_key,
    c.created_at,
    c._was_repaired
from `data_sentinel`.`silver`.`customer_history` c

-- join 1: the plan version valid on the day this customer version started

    on  c.plan_id = p.plan_id
    and c.valid_from >= p.valid_from
    and c.valid_from < p.valid_to
    and p.plan_key <> -1

-- join 2: the current version of the plan (used only if join 1 found nothing)

    select plan_id, plan_key
    from `data_sentinel`.`gold`.`dim_plan`
    where is_current = true and plan_key <> -1
) cp
    on c.plan_id = cp.plan_id

-- HELPER: find the customer behind a phone number.
-- Network usage, invoices and partner usage only know the (hashed) phone number, not the customer id.
-- If two customers share one phone number (a duplicate in the CRM), we pick the one with the lowest customer_id,
-- so every phone number points to exactly ONE customer and the facts never get duplicate rows.
-- The FIRST version of each customer is valid from 1900-01-01 here (not from created_at): invoices, payments and
-- partner usage can be older than the CRM record (e.g. July invoices for a customer created in September), and
-- they must still find their customer. Later versions keep their real dates, so history lookups are unchanged.

select
    c.customer_key,
    c.customer_id,
    c.msisdn_hash,
    case when c.valid_from = min(c.valid_from) over (partition by c.customer_id)
         then cast('1900-01-01' as timestamp) else c.valid_from end as valid_from,
    c.valid_to
from `data_sentinel`.`gold`.`dim_customer` c
join (
    select msisdn_hash, min(customer_id) as customer_id
    from `data_sentinel`.`gold`.`dim_customer`
    where customer_key <> -1
    group by msisdn_hash
) chosen
    on  c.msisdn_hash = chosen.msisdn_hash
    and c.customer_id = chosen.customer_id
where c.customer_key <> -1

-- FACT: one row per mobile app event.
-- The app sends the customer id directly, so we look up the customer VERSION valid at event time.
-- If no customer is found (or customer_id is empty), customer_key = -1.

select
    e.event_id,
    e.customer_id,
    e.event_type,
    e.app_version,
    e.event_ts,
    coalesce(c.customer_key, -1) as customer_key,
    to_date(e.event_ts) as event_date,
    cast(date_format(e.event_ts, 'yyyyMMdd') as int) as event_date_key,
    c.customer_key is not null as customer_known
from `data_sentinel`.`silver`.`app_event` e
left join `data_sentinel`.`gold`.`dim_customer` c
    on  c.customer_key <> -1
    and e.customer_id = c.customer_id
    and e.event_ts >= c.valid_from
    and e.event_ts < c.valid_to

select *
from `data_sentinel`.`gold`.`fact_app_events`
where customer_key is null

-- FACT: one row per partner usage record (roaming or international).
-- The partner file covers a whole month, so we look up the customer at the start of the NEXT month.
-- If no customer is found, customer_key = -1.

select
    p.partner_record_id,
    p.msisdn_hash,
    p.service,
    p.amount,
    p.currency,
    p.period_start,
    coalesce(c.customer_key, -1) as customer_key,
    c.customer_id,
    cast(date_format(p.period_start, 'yyyyMMdd') as int) as period_start_key,
    c.customer_key is not null as customer_known
from `data_sentinel`.`silver`.`partner_usage` p
left join `data_sentinel`.`gold_staging`.`int_customer_by_phone` c
    on  p.msisdn_hash = c.msisdn_hash
    and cast(add_months(p.period_start, 1) as timestamp) >= c.valid_from
    and cast(add_months(p.period_start, 1) as timestamp) < c.valid_to

-- FACT: one row per network record (a call, an SMS or a data session).
-- Inputs: silver.network_cdr, silver.customer_xref, and the customer lookup by phone number.
-- Each record gets the customer VERSION that was valid at the moment of the event.
-- If no customer is found, customer_key = -1 (unknown) so the record is still kept.

select
    u.cdr_id,
    u.msisdn_hash,
    u.event_type,
    u.event_ts,
    u.duration_sec,
    u.data_mb,
    u.cell_id,
    u.call_result,
    coalesce(c.customer_key, -1) as customer_key,
    c.customer_id,
    x.account_id,
    to_date(u.event_ts) as usage_date,
    cast(date_format(u.event_ts, 'yyyyMMdd') as int) as usage_date_key,
    c.customer_key is not null as customer_known
from `data_sentinel`.`silver`.`network_cdr` u

-- find the customer who owned this phone number at the time of the event
left join `data_sentinel`.`gold_staging`.`int_customer_by_phone` c
    on  u.msisdn_hash = c.msisdn_hash
    and u.event_ts >= c.valid_from
    and u.event_ts < c.valid_to

-- find the billing account of this phone number (only when CRM and billing match)
left join (
    select msisdn_hash, account_id
    from `data_sentinel`.`silver`.`customer_xref`
    where match_status = 'MATCHED'
) x
    on u.msisdn_hash = x.msisdn_hash

-- FACT: one row per invoice and source (billing_db or billing_file).
-- Each invoice gets the customer VERSION that was valid when the invoice was issued.
-- If no customer is found, customer_key = -1 (unknown) so the invoice is still kept.

select
    i.source,
    i.invoice_id,
    i.account_id,
    i.account_ref,
    i.msisdn_hash,
    i.period_start,
    i.period_end,
    i.plan_fee,
    i.overage,
    i.total_amount,
    i.status,
    i.issued_at,
    i.lines_total,
    i.lines_count,
    coalesce(c.customer_key, -1) as customer_key,
    c.customer_id,
    cast(date_format(i.period_start, 'yyyyMMdd') as int) as period_start_key,
    c.customer_key is not null as customer_known
from `data_sentinel`.`gold_staging`.`stg_invoices` i

-- invoice time = when it was issued; if that is empty, the last day of the billing period
left join `data_sentinel`.`gold_staging`.`int_customer_by_phone` c
    on  i.msisdn_hash = c.msisdn_hash
    and coalesce(i.issued_at, cast(i.period_end as timestamp)) >= c.valid_from
    and coalesce(i.issued_at, cast(i.period_end as timestamp)) < c.valid_to

    i.customer_id,
    i.account_id,

from `data_sentinel`.`gold_staging`.`stg_payments` p

-- Dashboard 3: one row per current customer with plan, billing, payments, network usage, app activity and partner usage.
-- Phone, email and name are masked; nothing raw reaches Gold.
with cust as (
    select * from `data_sentinel`.`gold`.`dim_customer` where is_current and customer_key <> -1
),
plan as (
    select plan_id, plan_name, monthly_fee, data_gb, voice_minutes from `data_sentinel`.`gold`.`dim_plan` where is_current and plan_key <> -1
),
inv as (
    select customer_id, count(*) as invoices, sum(total_amount) as billed_eur
    from `data_sentinel`.`gold`.`fact_invoice` where source = 'billing_db' and customer_key <> -1 group by customer_id
),
pay as (
    select customer_id,
           sum(case when status = 'PAID' then amount else 0 end) as paid_eur,
           max(case when status = 'PAID' then paid_at end) as last_payment_at
    from `data_sentinel`.`gold`.`fact_payment` where source = 'billing_db' and customer_key <> -1 group by customer_id
),
usage as (
    select customer_id,
           sum(case when event_type = 'VOICE' then duration_sec else 0 end) / 60.0 as voice_minutes_used,
           sum(case when event_type = 'SMS' then 1 else 0 end) as sms_count,
           sum(case when event_type = 'DATA' then data_mb else 0 end) as data_mb_used,
           sum(case when event_type = 'VOICE' and call_result = 'DROPPED' then 1 else 0 end) as dropped_calls,
           max(event_ts) as last_network_activity_at
    from `data_sentinel`.`gold`.`fact_usage` where customer_key <> -1 group by customer_id
),
app as (
    select customer_id,
           count(*) as app_events,
           sum(case when event_type = 'crash' then 1 else 0 end) as app_crashes,
           sum(case when event_type = 'plan_change' then 1 else 0 end) as plan_changes,
           max(case when event_type = 'login' then event_ts end) as last_login_at
    from `data_sentinel`.`gold`.`fact_app_events` where customer_key <> -1 group by customer_id
),
partner as (
    select customer_id, sum(amount) as partner_amount_eur
    from `data_sentinel`.`gold`.`fact_partner_usage` where customer_key <> -1 group by customer_id
)
select
    c.customer_id, c.name_masked, c.email_masked, c.msisdn_masked, c.city, c.country, c.status, c.created_at,
    p.plan_name, p.monthly_fee, p.data_gb as plan_data_gb, p.voice_minutes as plan_voice_minutes,
    coalesce(i.invoices, 0) as invoices,
    coalesce(i.billed_eur, 0) as billed_eur,
    coalesce(y.paid_eur, 0) as paid_eur,
    coalesce(i.billed_eur, 0) - coalesce(y.paid_eur, 0) as unpaid_eur,
    y.last_payment_at,
    coalesce(u.voice_minutes_used, 0) as voice_minutes_used,
    coalesce(u.sms_count, 0) as sms_count,
    coalesce(u.data_mb_used, 0) as data_mb_used,
    coalesce(u.dropped_calls, 0) as dropped_calls,
    u.last_network_activity_at,
    coalesce(a.app_events, 0) as app_events,
    coalesce(a.app_crashes, 0) as app_crashes,
    coalesce(a.plan_changes, 0) as plan_changes,
    a.last_login_at,
    coalesce(t.partner_amount_eur, 0) as partner_amount_eur
from cust c
left join plan p on c.plan_id = p.plan_id
left join inv i on c.customer_id = i.customer_id
left join pay y on c.customer_id = y.customer_id
left join usage u on c.customer_id = u.customer_id
left join app a on c.customer_id = a.customer_id
left join partner t on c.customer_id = t.customer_id
